label: Tesla BMS
info:
Claude Tesla BMS (TeslaBMS_Victron) - reads the JSON telemetry of the Teensy via USB.

1. On the Teensy: serial monitor, menu s -> m -> j (JSON on), q to save.
2. Check the serial port (default /dev/ttyACM0) in the 'Teensy USB' config node.
3. Needs node-red-node-serialport and @flowfuse/node-red-dashboard (Dashboard 2.0).
4. The port is found automatically (top of the flow); VE_SERVICE=ignore is set automatically.
5. Already have a Dashboard 2.0 base/theme? Then point the page 'Tesla BMS' at your own base and delete the imported ones.

info: Looks up the Teensy via /dev/serial/by-id (name contains 'Teensy'), sets the serial port via the serial control node and makes sure VenusOS serial-starter leaves the Teensy alone (udev rule VE_SERVICE=ignore for USB-ID 16c0:0483). The rule is also written to /data/rc.local so it comes back automatically after a firmware update.

name: find Teensys + ignore rule
command:
for P in $(ls /dev/serial/by-id/ 2>/dev/null | grep -i teensy); do echo "PORT=/dev/serial/by-id/$P"; done
R=/etc/udev/rules.d/zz-teslabms-teensy.rules
RW=/opt/victronenergy/swupdate-scripts/remount-rw.sh
if grep -q 0478 "$R" 2>/dev/null; then echo "UDEV=ok"; else [ -x "$RW" ] && "$RW" >/dev/null 2>&1; if printf '%s\n' 'ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="tty", ATTRS{idVendor}=="16c0", ATTRS{idProduct}=="0483", ENV{VE_SERVICE}="ignore"' 'SUBSYSTEM=="hidraw", ATTRS{idVendor}=="16c0", ATTRS{idProduct}=="0478", MODE="0666"' > "$R" 2>/dev/null; then udevadm control --reload-rules; udevadm trigger --action=add --subsystem-match=tty; echo "UDEV=added"; else echo "UDEV=noperm"; fi; fi
if grep -q teslabms-teensy-v2 /data/rc.local 2>/dev/null; then echo "RCLOCAL=ok"; elif [ -w /data/rc.local ] || { [ ! -e /data/rc.local ] && [ -w /data ]; }; then [ -f /data/rc.local ] || printf '#!/bin/sh\n' > /data/rc.local; sed -i '/teslabms-teensy/d' /data/rc.local; printf '%s\n' "# teslabms-teensy-v2: VE_SERVICE=ignore + bootloader access for the Teensy (comes back after a firmware update)" "grep -q 0478 $R 2>/dev/null || { [ -x $RW ] && $RW; printf '%s\\n' 'ACTION==\"add\", SUBSYSTEM==\"tty\", ATTRS{idVendor}==\"16c0\", ATTRS{idProduct}==\"0483\", ENV{VE_SERVICE}=\"ignore\"' 'SUBSYSTEM==\"hidraw\", ATTRS{idVendor}==\"16c0\", ATTRS{idProduct}==\"0478\", MODE=\"0666\"' > $R; udevadm control --reload-rules; udevadm trigger --action=add --subsystem-match=tty; } # teslabms-teensy" >> /data/rc.local; chmod +x /data/rc.local; echo "RCLOCAL=added"; else echo "RCLOCAL=noperm"; fi

label: Tesla BMS Test
info: Test bench: a second Teensy (e.g. a Teensy 4.0 with 1-2 modules) on another USB port of the GX, to test modules / CMUs. No CAN, no charger. The port is assigned automatically by 'Assign Teensy ports' in the tab 'Tesla BMS' (by USB serial number, saved in /data/home/nodered/.node-red/teslabms-teensy-roles.json). Updated together with the 'Tesla BMS' tab.
